title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: PMET retrenchment and unemployment
sections.summary: PMETs make up 57% of the resident workforce, over 70% of recent retrenchments, and most long-term unemployed, especially mature ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Today, 57% of our resident workforce are Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMETs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Although we have kept unemployment rates low and retrenchment declining the past three years, I am concerned with the fact that more than 70% of those retrenched the last three years were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: This is coupled with the fact that the majority of those classified as long-term unemployed are PMETs, especially the mature ones, and this group also found it much harder to rejoin the workforce after losing their jobs.

sections.label: Place-and-Train and PCPs
sections.summary: MOM said enhanced Place-and-Train schemes and Professional Conversion Programmes will help workers reskill and move into new occupations or sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: MOM shared that the enhanced Place-and-Train schemes and Professional Conversion Programmes will help more workers reskill and move into new occupations or sectors with progression.

sections.label: Union representation of executives
sections.summary: Unions seeking to represent executives met difficulties mainly because the exclusions in section 17(3) are worded too generally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: In the years that have followed, unions which have sought to extend their scope of representation to include executives have met with some difficulties, mainly due to the overly general way in which the exclusions in section 17(3) have been worded.

sections.label: Section 17(3) exclusions too broad
sections.summary: Unions find section 17(3) exclusions too broadly worded, letting employers claim mid-level executives fall within them though the law intended only senior management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The unions' experience, therefore, is that the exclusions set out in section 17(3) are too broadly worded, thereby giving employers the opportunity to claim that even mid-level executive employees fall within them, whereas the intent behind the law was only to exclude those who are at senior management levels and carrying out functions which genuinely give rise to a conflict of interest if they are represented by a union.

sections.label: FCF effectiveness and watchlist
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOM for an update on the FCF's effectiveness in levelling the playing field and eradicating nationality discrimination, and on the watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to ask MOM to provide an update on how effective the FCF has been in the past three years since implementation in levelling the playing field for our local PMEs and in eradicating "nationality" discrimination in hiring practices, including by employment and placement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I know the Minister has shared that we have nailed more than 300 companies into what MOM calls the "watchlist" where we see the "Triple Weak".

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Has there been an improvement since the last time the Minister shared about this "watchlist" and what kinds of companies, whether multinational corporations or small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and what sectors are these companies from?

sections.label: Bias against older workers
sections.summary: The speaker says unconscious bias against older workers is hard to detect and hopes the tripartite workgroup will look into minimising it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: There is an unconscious bias against older workers in general, although it is often difficult to detect such discrimination and gather evidence to prosecute and censure perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I hope the tripartite workgroup on older workers will also look into minimising, if not eradicating, this in the selection, recruitment, appraisal, promotion and even during retrenchments.

sections.label: Prison career counselling and reintegration
sections.summary: Career counselling, training, employment facilitation and reintegration should start in prison so offenders can seamlessly integrate back into the labour market and be gainfully employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Career counselling, training, employment facilitation and reintegration should start whilst they are in prison so that they can seamlessly integrate back into the labour market and be gainfully employed.

sections.label: Older PMETs, discrimination, ex-offenders
sections.summary: Older PMETs have higher re-employment and long-term unemployment rates than younger PMETs, and the passage raises ageism, assessing the FCF, zero tolerance for harassment, and opportunities for ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The re-employment rate and long-term unemployment rate of older PMETs are both higher than those of younger PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The second group refers to workers who are being discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: It has been three years since the FCF was implemented and there is a need to assess its efficacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I hope that the tripartite work group will pay attention to the issue of ageism when preparing their recommendation report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: We aim to create workplaces that adopt "zero tolerance" towards harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The fifth group are workers who are ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I urge employers not to view these ex-offenders with tinted glasses and give them opportunities to reintegrate into the workplace.

sections.label: Harassment cases and awareness efforts
sections.summary: MOM is asked to update on the number of harassment cases it addresses annually and on awareness efforts and measures to mitigate such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MOM update on the number of harassment cases that it addresses annually and what are the awareness efforts and measures to mitigate such cases?

sections.label: Expanding services as Work Pro
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider expanding such services to more companies as a form of Work Pro.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider expanding such services to more companies as a form of Work Pro?

sections.label: Effectiveness of e2i and MyCareersFuture
sections.summary: The passage asks how effective the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and MyCareersFuture are in helping jobseekers find a job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: How effective is the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and MyCareersFuture in helping them find a job?

sections.label: Adapt and Grow help for jobseekers
sections.summary: MOM is asked how the Adapt and Grow initiative and growth sectors effort have helped jobseekers take up new jobs, after residents said they had done everything advised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some of the residents have also said that they have already visited e2i and they have done everything that they have been advised to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, can MOM advise how has the Adapt and Grow (A&G) initiative and growth sectors effort helped jobseekers take up new jobs?

sections.label: Discriminatory practices and FCF watchlist
sections.summary: Asks how many companies still practise discrimination against Singaporeans and how many remain on the FCF watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: How many companies still carry out discriminatory practices against Singaporeans and how many are still on the FCF watchlist?

sections.label: MTI jobs-skills mismatch study
sections.summary: An MTI study using MyCareersFuture.sg data found generic and non-generic skills mismatches mattered, raising unsuccessful application probability by about 5.8%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our employers will waste resources seeking unreal matches, and the Government will not be spending effectively.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There has been one instructive study on jobs-skills mismatch by economists in the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) last November.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The study used data from MyCareersFuture.sg (MCF) platform and looked at the link between seven types of mismatches and job application outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Education, salary expectation and experience mismatches do not appear to be significant.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Rather, generic skills mismatch and non-generic skills mismatch mattered, with the latter mattering three times more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Both combined provided for about 5.8% increase in probability of an unsuccessful application.

sections.label: Measuring underemployment for policymaking
sections.summary: The International Conference of Labour Statisticians says measuring underemployment is necessary for better policymaking and evaluating employment policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the International Conference of Labour Statisticians, measuring underemployment is necessary for better policymaking, as it would improve the analysis of employment problems and contribute towards formulating and evaluating policies and initiatives to promote full, productive and freely chosen employment.

sections.label: Severely underemployed graduates and ITM manpower
sections.summary: A survey defined severely underemployed as full-time university graduates earning under $2,000 monthly, and 18 of 23 ITM industries would see manpower growth to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The survey came up with a matrix of three factors to identify "severely underemployed", that is, university graduates working full-time who were earning less than $2,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The OTC Institute suggested that it would be reasonable for the Government to target policies towards groups of severely underemployed persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, according to the Third Report of the Estimates Committee of Parliament released in October last year, 18 out of the 23 industries under the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) would see manpower growth up to 2030, while the remainder are not envisaged to experience any manpower growth up to the same period of time.

sections.label: Plans to encourage hiring older workers
sections.summary: Asks what Government plans beyond the SEC will encourage companies to transform and hire Singaporeans above 65, women, and part-time workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Apart from the Special Employment Credit (SEC), going forward, what are the Government's plans to prompt, support and encourage Singapore companies to accelerate the transformation of their business and HR processes to hire Singaporeans above the age of 65, provide higher salaries to attract Singaporean employees or successfully hire women, men or older workers who prefer part-time work as a result of needing time to look after children or their dependants, or for some other reasons?

sections.label: Self-employed share of workforce
sections.summary: Self-employed persons make up around 10% of Singapore's workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In Singapore, self-employed persons (SEPs) make up around 10% of the workforce.

sections.label: SEP MediSave contribute-as-you-earn
sections.summary: The Ministry is implementing the tripartite workgroup's recommendation of a contribute-as-you-earn model for SEPs' MediSave contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: The tripartite workgroup on SEPs released a set of recommendations last year recognising that most SEPs are self-employed as their preferred choice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Can MOM share the progress on the implementation of the recommendations as well as the impact on SEPs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry has indicated that it is working on implementing the tripartite working group's recommendation of a contribute-as-you-earn model for MediSave, whereby contribution to the self-employed worker’s MediSave account of the Central Provident Fund (CPF) is made as and when a service fee is earned.

sections.label: Incentives for SEP CPF contributions
sections.summary: A request asks the Ministry to consider incentives, including favourable tax treatment, for SEPs who voluntarily contribute to their CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry look into offering incentives for SEPs who voluntarily contribute to their Ordinary Account (OA), Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA) of CPF, including favourable tax treatment when they do so?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, many were concerned when the Minister recently stated three-quarters of CPF payouts are less than $500 a month.

sections.label: Divorce among women aged 40-59
sections.summary: The share of women aged 40-59 who were divorced rose from under 2.5% in 1980 to about 8% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While in 1980 less than 2.5% of women aged 40-59 were divorced, in 2018 about 8% were divorced.

sections.label: Ever-married women's number of children
sections.summary: In 1980 six in 10 ever-married women had four or more children, but by 2018 six in 10 had two or less.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1980, six in 10 ever-married women had four or more children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But by 2018, six in 10 had two or less.

sections.label: CPF contribution rate at age 55
sections.summary: CPF contribution rates drop by 11% overall at age 55, and a request asks for restoration to 37% for ages 55 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a Singaporean turns 55, their CPF contribution rate is drastically reduced by 11% overall.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have asked for the CPF contribution rate to be restored to the current rate of 37% in total, for ages 55 to 60.

sections.label: Review of senior employment steps
sections.summary: A call was made to review future steps for promoting senior employment after the re-employment age was raised to 67 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year, there was a call to review future steps for promoting senior employment after the move to raise the re-employment age to 67 was achieved in 2017.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: The WorkPro Job Redesign Grant of up to $300,000 helps companies change so workers above 50 can work more easily and safely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the WorkPro scheme, the Job Redesign Grant of up to $300,000 helps companies to make these changes so that workers aged above 50 can work more easily and safely.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Life expectancy rose from 76 in 1995 to 83 in 2017, and the question asks if the retirement and re-employment ages of 62 and 67 will be removed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Chairman, life expectancy has risen from 76 years in 1995 to 83 years in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: If the retirement age remains stuck at 62 years, Singaporeans who wish to continue working would be forced into early retirement for over two decades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Will the Government consider removing the artificial expiry date for productive senior workers, namely, the current retirement and re-employment ages of 62 and 67.

sections.label: Seniors' CPF monthly payouts
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question revealed 75% of seniors receive CPF monthly payouts under $500, and those 70 and older average below $300.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A recent Parliamentary Question revealed that 75% of these seniors receive CPF monthly payouts of less than $500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: And for those seniors 70 and older, the average monthly payouts dropped to below $300.

sections.label: Monetising a flat
sections.summary: After nine months with HDB, a woman understood monetising her flat and now has over $80,000 in cash and over $2,600 monthly CPF payout.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It took us nine months, working together with HDB, to help her understand the option of monetising her flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: She now lives a very different lifestyle, with a healthy cash balance of over $80,000 in her bank account, whilst receiving a monthly payout of over $2,600 from CPF.

sections.label: Triple weak companies watch list
sections.summary: The Minister for Manpower confirmed 250 companies were labelled triple weak, up from 100, and about 20 of the original 100 were removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In September last year, the Minister for Manpower confirmed that the Ministry was monitoring 250 companies labelled as "triple weak", up from the 100 in February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Out of the original 100 companies, about 20 were removed from the watch list as their HR practices had been raised to industry standards.

sections.label: TAFEP action and certificate verification
sections.summary: The passage asks what action TAFEP or the Ministry takes and notes not all employers verify certificates, as the Mikhy Farrera-Brochez case shows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I enquire what action the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) or the Ministry takes to deal with it and how does it educate such employers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, for educational certificates other than from India and China, where additional information is needed, not all employers perform independent verification with universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The case of Mikhy Farrera-Brochez, who forged his educational certificates, dramatically illustrates the limitations to this approach.

sections.label: Enforcement against EP kickback schemes
sections.summary: The passage asks what current enforcement mechanisms exist against kickback or false salary declaration schemes involving foreigners on EPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, what are the current enforcement mechanisms against kickback or false salary declaration schemes whereby foreigners on EPs are paid below the salary floor or pay a portion of their salaries back to the employer in some way?

sections.label: Full Retirement Sum withdrawal conditions
sections.summary: Members below 55 need at least S$166,000 in their accounts, and a 2017 amendment extended this to those with about S$83,000 plus a property pledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Members aged below 55 need to have the Full Retirement Sum of at least S$166,000 in their accounts, before they can do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: When the Act was amended in 2017, this provision was extended to members who had the required Basic Retirement Sum of about S$83,000, if they also had a sufficient property pledge or charge to make up the rest of the Full Retirement Sum.

sections.label: Auto payout at Payout Eligibility Age
sections.summary: The passage says public anger over a false PEA change shows support for setting auto payout at PEA by default.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The recent public disquiet over the allegation that CPF Board had quietly moved the Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) to 70, though unfounded, goes to show how much we look forward to the day when we can finally see and touch our CPF money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, any attempt to change that day, regardless of intention, will be met with disgust and anger, and rightly so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Thus, the call to set the auto payout at PEA by default should be considered seriously because it sends a clear message that the Government does not intend to and will not keep the members’ hard-earned savings beyond what is mandated by law.

sections.label: Tapping SA or RA for mortgage
sections.summary: The passage says residents needed to tap SA or RA to service mortgage arrears, but such requests were mostly rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, I wish to talk about balancing retirement and housing needs using CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I have residents who needed to tap into their SA or RA to help service their mortgage arrears, but such requests were mostly rejected.

sections.label: Members with low SA or RA
sections.summary: Some members in their late 40s or 50s have less than $10,000 standing in their SA or RA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Some of these members have less than $10,000 standing in their SA or RA, and they are already in their late 40s or 50s.

sections.label: Starting CPF payouts early
sections.summary: The passage says members should be allowed to do their own sums to decide if they need CPF payouts before retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: When that happens, our income will drop drastically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: We should allow members to do their own sums to determine if they need to start their CPF payouts early before retirement age.

sections.label: Defining special needs employment scope
sections.summary: Special needs individuals range widely, and the scope of those assistable for employment must be defined, eventually building a framework covering education, training and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Special needs individuals can be wide ranging, from those with varying levels of physical disabilities, to those with autism and attention disorder, and the other extreme spectrum for those with severe mental health challenges.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: We need to, first, clearly define the scope of special needs people that we are able to assist for work employment in the short term, and eventually to build a structured framework of assistance that looks into education, training and job prospects for them.

sections.label: Training special needs students skills
sections.summary: The speaker feels a more pressing need is training special needs individuals with specific industry skills while they are still schooling.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Apart from redesigning jobs and opening the employment doors of regular companies to those with special needs, I feel that a more pressing need and area that we have to focus on is the training of special needs individuals with specific skills for different industries when they are still schooling.

sections.label: Autism and attention disorder strengths
sections.summary: Studies show those with autism or attention deficit disorder have strengths in creative work, memory, Mathematics and computers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Looking at those with autism or attention deficit disorder, studies have shown that they exhibit strengths in many areas related to creative work, such as visual arts, music, self-contained direct tasks, and have strong memory, good in Mathematics and computer, amongst others.

sections.label: Government-funded employment programmes listed
sections.summary: Several Government-funded programmes help companies employ, train and integrate vulnerable persons or persons with special needs or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Chairman, there are currently several Government-funded programmes to help companies employ, train and integrate vulnerable persons or persons with special needs or disabilities, such as the Open Door Programme, SEC, Workfare Scheme, and Disability Management Programme.

sections.label: Support for employers hiring special needs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether more employer support, such as corporate tax relief, wage support or recognition, could be provided for hiring individuals with special needs or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Could more support for employers be provided, such as corporate tax relief or wage support when they hire individuals with special needs or disabilities, or giving employer recognition to companies that do so?

sections.label: PWD employment barriers in Singapore
sections.summary: In 2017 only five in 100 PWDs in Singapore were officially working, with barriers including employer unwillingness, lack of trained PWDs and agency resource restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Kudos to them, numerous PWDs have been gainfully employed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It has been reported that in 2017, only five in 100 PWDs in Singapore are officially working, and this is quoted as one of the lowest in developed nations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Key barriers are several: one, an unwillingness of potential employers caused by stigmatisation and reluctance to redesign job processes; two, the lack of a large enough pipeline of trained PWDs upstream; and three, an inability to focus and scale by agencies, such as SG Enable, due to resource restrictions.

sections.label: Inclusive employment and workplace fatalities
sections.summary: The passage asks MOM about incentives for inclusive employers, making the SEC for PWDs permanent, and how Singapore compares on workplace fatality rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Start with a minimum 1% target for large employers with staff strengths of more than 1,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will MOM provide more incentives for inclusive employers such as: one, making the SEC for PWDs a permanent feature so that employers are assured of ongoing support; and two, increasing this amount or make it an inclusivity allowance to the employer so that beyond subsidising the CPF of its workers with special needs, the employer can also pay for job coaching services?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share how does Singapore fare when compared against other developed countries, in terms of reducing our workplace fatality rate?

sections.label: Differentiated insurance premiums for WSH
sections.summary: The passage calls for differentiated insurance premiums to deter companies with poor WSH records, noting fatalities fell in 2018 but injuries rose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, I called for differentiated insurance premiums to increase the cost to companies with poor WSH track record as a deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Although workplace fatalities have dropped to an all-time low in 2018, the number of major and minor injuries has actually increased.

sections.label: Mandatory trained WSH representatives
sections.summary: The passage cites 2018 National WSH Statistics showing low-risk sectors had accidents and urges tripartite partners to support mandatory trained WSH representatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The 2018 National WSH Statistics have shown that even low-risk sectors were not spared from workplace accidents and injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There is no room for complacency in WSH and, therefore, I urge our tripartite partners to support making it a mandatory requirement for every company to have a trained WSH representative, to make WSH more pervasive in our workplaces.

sections.label: National WSH Training Academy
sections.summary: The passage states the National WSH Training Academy can help ensure high and consistent WSH standards across sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The National WSH Training Academy can help ensure high and consistent WSH standards across sectors.

sections.label: UK insolvency salary claims
sections.summary: The passage states that in the UK, workers of insolvent companies can claim outstanding salaries from the National Insurance Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the UK, if a company is insolvent and the workers' employment has been terminated, the workers can claim for part or all their outstanding salaries out of the National Insurance Fund (NIF) which is paid by employees, employers and the self-employed.

sections.label: Migrant worker training and payments
sections.summary: The passage gives Work Permit holder numbers, proposes a national training framework for migrant workers, and hopes to mandate electronic salary payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: As at June 2018, we have more than 950,000 Work Permit holders working in Singapore, with more than 280,000 of them in the construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The Government should consider implementing a national training and skills recognition framework, similar to WSQ, for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: For foreign domestic workers (FDW), the Labour Movement hopes to obtain the MOM's support to expand the pilot skills certification programme offered by the Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE) to further improve the employment ecosystem for FDWs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: One area which the Migrant Workers' Centre and CDE have been focusing on in recent years is to encourage employers to adopt electronic salary payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: We have seen some encouraging results thus far, and I hope that the Government can consider mandating electronic salary payments to migrant workers, to prevent cases of employer abuse.

sections.label: Migrant worker job placement
sections.summary: These factors cause persistently low successful job placement for vulnerable workers, and the speaker hopes Government works with NTUC to improve support for migrant workers in disputes with bad employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: These factors contribute to a persistently low rate of successful job placement for this group of vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can continue to work with NTUC to improve the migrant worker employment system such that there is better end-to-end support for migrant workers involved in disputes with bad employers.

sections.label: Employers cutting recruitment fees
sections.summary: Some local employers purportedly take a cut of recruitment fees, incentivising hiring new workers instead of retaining experienced foreign workers, compounded by a 14-day re-employment window.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Some local employers purportedly take a cut of recruitment fees which incentivises them to hire new workers instead of retaining foreign workers already in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: This means that workers who have gained skills and experience and are better socialised to our society are sent home, thus lost to our economy in favour of a continuous influx of inexperienced and low-skilled foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: The problem is compounded by the short window period of 14 days to seek re-employment.

sections.label: Workplace stress and mental health
sections.summary: Ninety percent of psychological conditions in Singaporean adults root from workplace stress, yet only 51% of employers have emotional and psychosocial programmes despite 72% seeing stress as a productivity issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Ninety percent of psychological conditions in Singaporean adults have their root cause in workplace stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: What is perhaps most striking is that even as 72% of employers in Singapore consider stress and mental health an issue which affects productivity, only 51% have emotional and psychosocial programmes in place.

sections.label: Women leaving technology after pregnancy

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the number of women entering the technology sector is not sizeable to begin with, attrition rises sharply after pregnancy and childcare.

sections.label: SUTD women enrolment target

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At SUTD, we make concerted efforts to maintain a 40% women enrolment in our engineering and architecture programmes.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit for women

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our SkillsFuture Credit programme can certainly help women to upskill.

sections.label: Funding research on women's careers
sections.summary: Calls for funding longitudinal research on women's career trajectories to understand attrition and re-entry, aiding efforts against female under-representation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More importantly, can we fund systematic longitudinal research that tracks the career trajectories of women through various industry sectors so that we can better understand their reasons for attrition as well as the factors that promote re-entry into the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is only with robust evidence that we can take a more proactive approach to ameliorating this problem of female under-representation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are investments that Singapore can and should make not just for women but for our society as a whole.

sentences.text: Has this resulted in better employee outcomes, such as better employee well-being, greater worker productivity and, hence, better business performance for employers?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, working closely with the International Labour Organization to develop suitable methodologies.

sentences.text: Second, the re-employment age remains useful and should also go up beyond 67.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister has announced that the DRC for the services sector will be tightened from next year.

sections.label: SME transformation and job redesign
sections.summary: The Government will help SMEs transform, improve productivity and redesign jobs to attract Singaporeans and spread manpower risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Where can our companies get their workers then?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hence, should we not redesign some of these jobs so that they become acceptable to local workers and, at the same time, spread out manpower risks?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Hence, if we consider this from a longer-term perspective, we have had no choice but to accelerate the pace of transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I have this to say to the SMEs: let the Government help you and walk with you on this transformation journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will help you improve productivity, and assist you in redesigning some of the jobs to attract Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, there are many solutions in the market which are applicable for the services sector, and can help businesses transform successfully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I believe that as long as we combine the tenacity and fighting spirit of our companies and the multi-pronged assistance from the Government, our SMEs will be able to progress further and emerge stronger in the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, earlier, I spoke about how MOM uplifts the wages and skills of our lower-income workers through a mutually reinforcing system of different support measures while maintaining a tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We also want to nurture an inclusive and caring society that will enable all workers to thrive and have meaningful opportunities at work.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit for special needs
sections.summary: Employers of Singaporeans with special needs receive SEC and ASEC wage offsets, extended one more year until 2020 and reviewed alongside mainstream schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Members would be pleased to know that employers of Singaporeans with special needs receive the Special Employment Credit (SEC) that provides wage offsets of up to 16% of the employee's monthly income, regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the Additional SEC (ASEC), employers of Singaporeans with special needs aged 67 and above receive wage offsets of up to 22% of the employee's monthly income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: These rates are already two times the highest rates of the mainstream schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, the SEC and ASEC for Singaporeans with special needs will also be extended for one more year until 2020 and reviewed for the longer term, alongside the mainstream schemes, as announced at Budget.

sections.label: Special needs placements through programmes

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In the past three years, more than 1,600 persons with special needs have been placed through these programmes.

sections.label: Tsu-fei ODP Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: Tsu-fei tapped ODP's Job Redesign Grant, which supports 90% of job redesign costs of up to $20,000 per employee with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Tsu-fei tapped on ODP's Job Redesign Grant, which supports 90% of job redesign costs of up to $20,000 per employee with special needs.

sections.label: Career Trial for special needs
sections.summary: Career Trial lets employers and persons with special needs try out job fit, with training allowances, salary support and retention incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To address these, Career Trial provides opportunities for employers and persons with special needs to try out each other and make a better assessment of job fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: During the trial, which can be up to three months, jobseekers will receive a training allowance from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And to encourage hiring and retention of persons with special needs, employers receive salary support after the trial, while persons with special needs who are hired and stay for at least three months receive retention incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MOM and SG Enable will be releasing a Job Redesign Guide by the first half of this year.

sentences.text: The Employment Claims Tribunals (ECTs) can order employers to pay owed salaries to employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If lower-income workers are unable to recover their claims via WSS, they can receive financial assistance from the Short-Term Relief Fund (STRF).

sentences.text: Employers who do so can be liable to a maximum fine of $30,000 or up to two years’ jail, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, in 2018, 46 agencies and employers were taken to task for kickback-related offences.

sentences.text: The period of employment can now extend up to 26 years for skilled Work Permit holders in selected sectors.

sentences.text: Our workplace fatality rate declined from 2.2 per 100,000 workers in 2010 to 1.2, or a record low of 41 fatal cases, in 2018, last year.

sections.summary: MOM will increase the Work-Life Grant budget from $30 million to $100 million, and MOM and SNEF are developing a job-sharing implementation guide for employers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In Parliament last month, I mentioned that the Work-Life Grant has received healthy application numbers since its launch, and the Government is exploring increases to the Work-Life Grant budget to make FWA adoption more pervasive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that MOM will increase the Work-Life Grant budget to a total of $100 million from the current $30 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As job-sharing is less well-known and practised amongst employers today, MOM and SNEF are developing a job-sharing implementation guide for employers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)

sentences.text: As of end January 2019, about 1,300 employers employing 400,000 employees have adopted the Standard.

sections.label: Types of workplace harassment
sections.summary: Egregious cases like outrage of modesty and stalking are offences under the Penal Code and POHA, while other harassment may not meet legal thresholds but still distresses employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: One, egregious cases, for example, like the outrage of modesty and stalking, belong to the class of conduct which constitutes offences under the Penal Code and the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The other type of harassment pertains to behaviour that may not fall under the legal threshold for criminal investigations or civil recourse under POHA, but nonetheless distresses and affects employees, for example, actions without the intention to cause, and are unlikely to cause harassment, alarm or distress to a specific employee, but which may still cause discomfort and affect other employees.

sections.label: TAFEP workplace harassment resource centre
sections.summary: TAFEP will be a help and resource centre for workplace harassment, providing advice and resources including a video, sample policy and training provider list.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In this regard, I am pleased to announce that TAFEP will now be a help and resource centre for workplace harassment for both employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Besides providing advice, TAFEP will provide a host of resources on its website that includes a new introductory video on how to manage workplace harassment; a sample Workplace Harassment Prevention Policy that companies can incorporate in their HR policies; and a list of training providers employers may engage to train their supervisors in managing workplace harassment.

sections.label: Job applicants' unrelated information
sections.summary: Employers should not ask job applicants for information unrelated to the employee's ability for the position, such as pre-existing medical history including mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Employers should not ask job applicants for information unrelated to the employee’s ability for the position, such as pre-existing medical history, including mental health conditions.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant budget increase
sections.summary: MOM will increase the Work-Life Grant budget from $30 million to $100 million and extend the application period by three years until June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To make FWA adoption more pervasive, MOM will increase the Work-Life Grant budget from the current $30 million to $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In addition, the application period for the Grant will also be extended by three years until June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I hope more companies can benefit from the Grant and support their employees’ FWA adoption, including women, older workers, caregivers and PMETs on job-sharing.

sections.label: Tripartite partners to look into it

sentences.text: The tripartite partners will be looking into it.

sections.label: LED scheme and rebranding support
sections.summary: MOM is willing to help companies under the LED scheme and supports rebranding.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to the second question, if the company has a commitment, they want to find ways to become leaner and they are prepared to come under the Lean Enterprise Development (LED) scheme, we will be very willing to see how to help.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To the first question on rebranding, absolutely yes.

sections.label: Job quality must improve
sections.summary: Job quality, work content, conditions, hours and terms must all improve.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The actual job quality, the content of the work, the way the work is carried out, the work conditions, the hours and also the terms, all these must improve.

sections.label: Lowering DRC for services
sections.summary: They support lowering the DRC for services to reduce reliance on foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a matter of principle, we support the lowering of the DRC for services, as we feel that we should reduce our over-reliance on foreign manpower where we can.

sections.label: Retirement adequacy for women reviewed
sections.summary: Retirement adequacy is continuously reviewed, and the average CPF balance for women has grown slightly faster than for men.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is certainly an area that will continuously be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But, perhaps to address the Member's question on the retirement adequacy for women in general, not just those who are involved in caregiving roles, in fact, over the last 10 years, the average CPF balance for women has been growing slightly faster than for men.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, if you compound it over time, compared to the men's 7.6%, the gap is closing.

sections.label: Female employment rate 25 to 64
sections.summary: The female employment rate for those aged 25 to 64 is currently 72%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Currently, our female employment rate for those aged 25 to 64 is at 72%.

sections.label: Technology and Work-Life Grant
sections.summary: Technology can help redesign rank-and-file and PMET jobs, and the Work-Life Grant was enhanced last year to support PMET job-sharing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We can now leverage technology as an enabler to help us redesign jobs for both rank-and-file and PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This was why the Work-Life Grant was enhanced last year to provide better support for job-sharing at PMET-levels.

sections.label: CPF payouts and fixed deposits
sections.summary: Members can withdraw payouts anytime from 65, and unclaimed fixed deposits are rolled over because they earn more money.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members can withdraw their payouts anytime from 65.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If he does not instruct us, we roll over his FD because it earns him more money.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we do not do that but, instead, the moment he turns 65, I terminate his FD and let his savings go into the Current Account, which earns much less interest, it will cause him to earn less money.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant and FWA adoption
sections.summary: MOM efforts to promote workplace well-being include raising the Work-Life Grant from S$30 million to S$100 million and increased FWA adoption.

sections.label: Silver Support and CPF payouts
sections.summary: The Member asks how far lower-income seniors qualifying for Silver Support and their CPF are from the $700 Basic Retirement Sum monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The first is that I asked during my cut for the lower-income seniors where they have little family support, they qualify for Silver Support, they do not own a property to unlock, and I know the previous answers were that if their CPF is very low, they get Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask – and I asked it in my cut – if you combine those who qualify for Silver Support and their CPF, how far are they from the $700 of Basic Retirement Sum per month?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: If we add up the CPF monthly payout plus the Silver Support, how much would they get?
